chapter_title: Chương 85: 0085【Mã Đề Nhanh Gió Xuân Đắc Ý】

segments.title: Chương 85: 0085【Mã Đề Nhanh Gió Xuân Đắc Ý】
segments.content:
Late July.

Principal Yan personally drove to the countryside to deliver the acceptance letter, followed by City Daily's Reporter Yuan's car.

Wu Meng lived in the county town, so he had already delivered hers in the morning. In the afternoon, he headed straight for Chen Guiliang's house.

In the end, Wu Meng hadn't dared to apply for the Yuanpei Program; that thing was just too unpredictable.

"Scraaaape~"

The sound of the car's undercarriage scraping came from below, but Principal Yan wasn't bothered in the least, driving at high speed on the bumpy county road.

This year, of the four students in the city admitted to Tsinghua or Peking University, No. 2 High School accounted for two of them.

The car turned onto a village road. It was scorching hot, and no villagers were in sight.

Spotting a house not far from the road, Principal Yan got out of the car and walked over under the blazing sun. Standing outside a family's courtyard, he called out, "Is anyone home? Excuse me, is anyone here?"

Reporter Yuan didn't get out of the car. It was too hot.

His task today was simple: take a photo of Principal Yan delivering the acceptance letter to Chen Guiliang.

A village woman walked to the door of the main house. "Who are you looking for?"

Principal Yan said, "I'm here to deliver Chen Guiliang's university acceptance letter. He got into Peking University."

The village woman hurried out of the courtyard and shouted into the distance, "Fourth Grandpa, Second Auntie, your grandson got into Peking University! The acceptance letter is here!"

The villagers, who could only stay home and sleep in the heat, all came out of their houses upon hearing this shout.

The maternal grandfather and grandmother rushed over even faster.

"Greetings, elders. I'm the principal of No. 2 High School, here to deliver your grandson's acceptance letter," Principal Yan said with a smile.

"Great, great, hello, Principal!"

The grandfather quickly extended an invitation, "The sun is scorching and it's terribly hot. Please come inside for a cup of tea, Principal."

Principal Yan said, "No, thank you. I'm just here to ask for directions."

"I'll take you there!" the grandmother said hurriedly.

The younger maternal uncle was playing cards. He and his card-playing friends rushed over. Principal Yan simply had all three of them get in his car.

A few villagers, undeterred by the sun, trotted along to watch the excitement.

Most villagers, however, returned home to escape the heat. From time to time, the sound of a parent scolding a child would emerge from a house: "Look at Chen Guiliang, he got into Peking University! What are you doing at school? Hurry up and do your summer homework!"

The few villagers who followed along spread the word as they went, and the village head and other cadres also hurried over upon hearing the news.

Chen Guiliang was at home, reading a history of the Ming Dynasty and continuing to copy down useful information.

Then he heard a commotion from behind the house.

His younger cousin Chen Guirong's voice was the loudest. "Brother, the letter is here! The Peking University acceptance letter is here!"

Chen Guiliang hadn't even moved before his parents rushed outside.

His grandmother, usually calm and composed, also seemed very excited now, standing under the eaves and constantly looking out.

Principal Yan and Reporter Yuan arrived, surrounded by a crowd of villagers. Chen Guiliang went forward to shake their hands and introduced his parents and grandmother.

His grandfather had also arrived by this time, but Chen Guiliang pretended not to see him.

Principal Yan shook hands with Chen Guiliang's elders again, smiling in admiration. "You have worked hard, raising such a talent for our country!"

His parents and grandmother instantly beamed with joy.

Principal Yan took out the acceptance letter and handed it to Chen Guiliang personally. "Student Chen Guiliang, I wish you continued success in your university studies. Strive to make new contributions to our country and its people!"

Reporter Yuan stepped back a few paces and clicked the shutter, taking a photo.

Looking at the dilapidated state of Chen Guiliang's house, an idea suddenly struck him. He pulled Principal Yan aside and said, "How about we find a different spot for the photo? For example, a patch of dry farmland, with Chen Guiliang holding a hoe, working under the hot sun to help his family. Principal Yan, you can stand in the field too, handing the acceptance letter to this rural student."

Principal Yan thought it was a brilliant idea and gestured for Chen Guiliang to come over.

Chen Guiliang was speechless when he heard the proposal. "It's 40 degrees Celsius. What farmer would be working in this weather?"

Reporter Yuan said, "News is also an art. Art originates from life but transcends it. You usually help your family with farm work, don't you?"

"Yes, sometimes I do," Chen Guiliang replied.

Reporter Yuan said, "Then it's not fabrication. What we're going to show is something you've done before. It's just that you're not doing it today because it's too hot. This is called a reenactment!"

Chen Guiliang thought to himself: *I also majored in journalism in my last life. What kind of bullshit are you spouting?*

Chen Guiliang shook his head repeatedly. "Let's not. This isn't a good idea."

Reporter Yuan thought the young man was just shy, so he went to discuss it with Chen Guiliang's parents.

The onlooking villagers heard the conversation and all encouraged Chen Guiliang to do the "reenactment."

"Just go take the picture in the fields. You often carry water."

"Don't be scared, we won't say anything."

"Listen to the reporter, hurry up and get a picture in the fields."

"..."

The villagers spoke lightheartedly, laughing and joking. No one took it seriously, and they even found the idea of everyone putting on a show quite amusing.

Everyone except Chen Guiliang supported Reporter Yuan.

Chen Guiliang had no choice but to go along with their performance. The city newspaper was only distributed locally anyway. Besides, ordinary citizens didn't read it, and no one at government offices and institutions read their subscribed copies either.

It was a newspaper with sales figures but no readers!

Holding a hoe, Chen Guiliang went to the fields to take a picture with Principal Yan.

Reporter Yuan then had the family of four, plus the maternal grandfather and grandmother, stand in front of their dilapidated house for a group photo. Chen Guiliang stood in the middle holding the acceptance letter, with the elders on either side and behind him.

Principal Yan said to the elders, "Tomorrow, there will be a parade through the county town with big red flowers. You should all come along."

Grandma couldn't go; she got carsick.

Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan joyfully agreed.

The grandfather asked, "Can we go too?"

"You can all go," said Principal Yan. "One large bus for the two students and their parents will have more than enough room for everyone."

The younger maternal uncle asked, "Can I go too?"

"Everyone can go," said Principal Yan.

A villager immediately joked, "Hey, San'guaizi, you can't even walk straight, and you want to join the parade with a big red flower?"

The younger maternal uncle puffed out his chest. "My nephew is going to Peking University, why can't I go?"

Chen Guiliang smiled and looked at Chen Xingmin. "Second Uncle and Guirong should come too."

He only invited his second uncle and cousin, not his second aunt or grandfather.

"Sounds good," Chen Xingmin said with a grin.

The second aunt was quite unhappy but still said to her son, "You need to learn from your older brother. When you get to high school, don't just fool around!"

"Okay, okay," the cousin replied with his head down.

"Dong dong dong qiang!"

The sound of gongs and drums came from the other side of the mountain pass. The village cadres, leading some villagers who weren't afraid of the heat, were actually beating gongs and drums as they headed towards Chen Guiliang's house.

Chen Guiliang felt a bit embarrassed, but also... quite thrilled!

Principal Yan winked at Reporter Yuan, then smiled and went to greet them. "Hello, I am Yan Shunde, the principal of No. 2 High School."

"Hello, Principal Yan," the village head extended both hands for a firm handshake. "I'm the village head, Chen Xingyao, from the same ancestral hall and generation as Chen Guiliang's father. Thank you and the school's leaders and teachers for cultivating our Guiliang into such a promising young man!"

Chen Guiliang smiled without saying anything. He didn't have a very good impression of the village head.

Principal Yan said, "It was also thanks to your support. It's not easy for a child from the countryside to make it."

Reporter Yuan directed them, "Move a little closer with the gongs and drums. Principal Yan and the village head, stand in the middle and shake hands... Yes, yes, keep smiling..."

As they chatted, the village head brought up the thing he was most proud of in his life. "I used to be a soldier, you know. Enlisted in '68."

"My respects, my respects," Principal Yan replied perfunctorily.

But the village head latched onto him, continuously pulling Principal Yan into conversation, even mentioning that his own nephew was planning to apply to No. 2 County High School.

More and more villagers arrived upon hearing the news, each finding a shady spot and gathering in small groups to chat.

Chen Guiliang's elders were also surrounded, chatting away. The occasional compliments made their faces glow with pride.

In the evening, his parents, maternal grandparents, second uncle, younger maternal uncle, and cousin all stayed with Chen Guiliang at a hotel in the county town, waiting for the celebratory parade the next day.

Principal Yan's car couldn't fit everyone on the way to the county town, but luckily Reporter Yuan helped out with his car.

Unfortunately, Grandma couldn't come because of her motion sickness.

The next morning, several leaders from the county education bureau arrived. Chen Guiliang and Wu Meng, along with their families, headed to the main auditorium.

It was particularly embarrassing; the two of them had to wear big red flowers on their chests.

However, all their relatives and elders were laughing heartily. Chen Guiliang's parents even struck up a casual conversation with Wu Meng's parents as if they were old friends.

Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan felt like their lives were now complete and didn't think about anything else. They couldn't be bothered to open a rabbit farm anymore; they would just farm in the countryside for the rest of their lives.

A cameraman from the city television station was there, and the city newspaper reporter was also taking pictures.

First, there were speeches from the leaders, recounting the glorious history of the county and the school, lavishing praise on the two outstanding students, and then looking forward to a bright future...

Then, Chen Guiliang and Wu Meng, wearing their big red flowers, went on stage to receive award plaques from the leaders.

Wu Meng received more prize money because she was the city's top scorer. The education bureau awarded her 10,000 yuan, and the school awarded 30,000 yuan.

Chen Guiliang received less: 8,000 yuan from the education bureau and 20,000 yuan from the school.

It was nothing compared to later years, but it was quite good for the time.

The real estate boom hadn't started yet, and local government finances were extremely tight!

"Bang bang bang bang bang!"

The sound of firecrackers erupted.

The students taking summer cram classes, who were about to enter their third year of high school, looked up at the sound.

The teachers in a few of the classes said directly to their students, "Go on out and have a look. Your seniors are being honored today. I hope that next year, some of you will receive the same treatment."

The students cheered and ran out of the classrooms. Seeing the spectacle was secondary; the main thing was that they didn't have to attend this class anymore.

The repeating students had also started their cram classes.

"Aren't you going to have a look?" Qin Shanshan asked.

Yang Hao smiled awkwardly. "I'd better not go."

Qin Shanshan looked at the other repeaters and saw that most of them hadn't moved.

Others were celebrating with big red flowers while they were re-studying in the repeater class. They hadn't quite adjusted their mindset yet.

Qin Shanshan ran over by herself. When she saw them, she felt too shy to say anything, only watching her two former classmates from a distance.

She used to be carefree, but now she was finally moved by something.

Chen Guiliang and Wu Meng walked at the very front, followed by the leaders, with the parents and relatives at the back. They walked from the auditorium to the school gate to get on the bus, with firecrackers being set off three times along the way.

Some of the summer school students chased after them, and some even laughingly shouted, "Great Hero Chen."

Chen Guiliang's fame far surpassed that of Wu Meng, the top scorer!

Everyone boarded a brand-new bus, which drove from the school to the main road of the county town, then circled to the old town, and made another loop to the new district.

Firecrackers popped and crackled along the way.

The front and back of the bus were decorated with big red flowers and red celebratory banners.

An electronic loudspeaker continuously broadcasted: "A warm congratulations to..."

Chen Guiliang and Wu Meng were seated at the front of the bus, on the left and right sides respectively, so that passersby could admire them.

In reality, there were hardly any people on the streets.

Who would go out in such hot weather?

Younger cousin Chen Guirong was particularly impressed. No. 2 High School's campus was so big, and his older brother was so magnificent. And there was so much prize money!

He now felt that vocational school was pointless; it was more useful to attend high school and go to university.

The next day, Chen Guiliang went to the city to collect more prize money.

This time, it was a local private business owner (a real estate developer) giving out the money. For the four students in the city admitted to Tsinghua or Peking University, each received a reward of 20,000 yuan.

Chen Guiliang's college entrance exam score was finally revealed.

The West China City Daily was the first to publish an article: Genius Literary Youth Chen Guiliang Can Get into Peking University Even Without Special Admission!

The newspaper didn't care if he could actually get in; as long as he passed Peking University's admission score threshold, it was good enough.

(What do you mean, forcibly raising the main character's score? All the previous chapters that gave his test scores, and the chapter about the exam room that mentioned the reform of the liberal arts comprehensive paper, were all setting up for the main character to get super high scores in Chinese and liberal arts comprehensive in the college entrance exam. Don't make random comments if you're just skipping through.)

(Some people also question this and that, but it was all explained in the first chapter or two. Some things were even explained clearly in the first two paragraphs of a chapter, I don't know why they can't see it. We've already written up to the 2004 college entrance exam, and there are still people asking if SARS is about to happen.)
